answer: An AI agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a proof-of-stake identity kernel that demands a slashable bond before any vote or payout. The kernel ties one deposit to one identity, so cloning one agent into a thousand wallets needs a thousand funded deposits, not merely a thousand keys. Once an attacker's budget hits its nadir, forging more faces costs more than buying honest stake. A sudden comet swarm of fresh accounts still dies at the gate, since every new skin needs capital that is slashed the moment fraud is detected.
